Chinese national rescued from tunnel in Nepal 10 days after catastrophic flooding. Rescuers in Nepal pulled a Chinese national alive on Saturday from a tunnel buried by debris, as emergency response teams dug with new vigour in the search for missing people 10 days after catastrophic flooding. A joint rescue team comprising personnel from the Nepal Army and foreign experts rescued the man from 225 metres inside the tunnel of the Upper Trishuli-1 Hydropower Project in Rasuwa district, a military statement said. A picture of the rescue published on the army’s Facebook page shows the man, identified only as Luhaitao, with his arms around the shoulders of two camouflage-clad rescuers. He looked alert but his hands were covered in thick, slimy mud. “His health is currently being assessed and further search and rescue operations are continuing,” the army said. The survivor was among hundreds of hydropower workers who went missing since a tsunami-like wall of water and mud swept through the China-Nepal border following a vast glacial and rock collapse on August 26. Two Nepali hydropower workers were rescued on Friday at the Trishuli 3A tunnel, where searches continued alongside multiple other sites, with at least 12 hydropower projects destroyed by the floods. So far, 1,344 bodies have been recovered in Nepal, according to the national disaster agency, with around 5,000 people missing. In China, state media said 31 people had been killed and 531 were missing. That takes the overall death toll to 1,375 people, and more than 5,500 missing. Thousands in relief camps Army spokesman Raja Ram Basnet told AFP that “work is underway at the tunnels” to locate any survivors. The government initially said it believed more than 100 workers could be alive inside multiple tunnels. Rescuers called it a “miracle” after the two Nepali men, caked in mud, were pulled out alive on Friday, nine days after being trapped by the flood. They were taken to hospital and are said to be in a stable condition. Experts from India, China, Australia and South Korea have been aiding Nepali rescuers in their search of survivors inside blocked tunnels. With morgues overflowing, some 1,030 bodies had been buried in mass graves after taking DNA samples for future identification, Nepal Police said on Saturday. Prime Minister Balendra Shah promised to provide “safe and comfortable accommodation” for thousands of people displaced by the disaster and currently living in temporary relief camps. “We know that staying there [in camps] is not easy for you,” he said in a Friday post on social media. But he promised to “once again create an environment where you can dream about and build your future”.

Police charge sheet says building management at fault for Gul Plaza inferno. KARACHI: Police on Saturday submitted a charge sheet before the South judicial magistrate on the Gul Plaza fire, blaming the building management’s “negligence”. The deadly inferno , which erupted on the night of January 17 at the mall and took nearly two days to be fully extinguished , had claimed at least 73 lives and left over 1,100 shops in ruins. A previous charge sheet submitted in July had named six people — including 11-year-old Huzaifa — as the accused. However, a judicial magistrate had rejected the document, noting that the investigating officer (IO) had not conducted a thorough and satisfactory probe. The fresh charge sheet, dated September 3 and submitted by the Nabi Bux police, names four of those six as the accused sent for trial: Huzaifa’s father Naimatullah who owned an artificial flower shop; Gul Plaza Traders Association President Tanveer Pasta; and association members Ammar Ismail and Muhammad Ramzan. Meanwhile, regarding the role of authorities, the charge sheet said the fire brigade, Rescue 1122, and Karachi Metropolitan Corporation (KMC) “used the resources they had with great efforts to put out the blaze”. Listing the faults on the building management’s side, the document stated that the Gul Plaza administration lacked adequate tools to extinguish the fire, considering the scale of the building. It added that there was “no alternative arrangement for emergency lights, due to which people faced difficulties leaving” the building. It noted that during the investigation, the complainant in the case said only two of the building’s gates were open at the time of the fire. “People could not leave due to the locks on the iron gates,” the charge sheet read. It went on to say that during the rescue operation, it was discovered that the iron gates on the third floor were padlocked, which “showed that the Gul Plaza administration had their guards close them”. The document further pointed out that the building management had K-Electric switch off the power supply “despite knowing that they do not have any other alternative arrangement for lighting”. The charge sheet said Faisal Ibrahim, the owner of Fire Works VIP Service, used to buy the fire safety equipment for the Gul Plaza union. It added that during the investigation, the quantity of such equipment was found to be inadequate, and that the building management was responsible for repairing and replenishing it. This proved the “criminal negligence and carelessness” of the building management, the charge sheet declared. It recalled that the findings of the Sindh government’s inquiry commission and the judicial commission also proved the Gul Plaza administration’s negligence. It noted that safety equipment and speakers were not used, while the exits were also found closed. On the other hand, the charge sheet recalled the rescue operation and the death of a firefighter in the process. It added, “Due to these reasons, the hard work of the rescue services cannot be doubted, and no concrete testimony emerged during the investigation that would show criminal negligence of rescue authorities.” The charge sheet highlighted that neither the government inquiry body nor the judicial commission found rescue authorities at fault for any criminal negligence. While departmental action was taken against Civil Defence Director Abdul Majeed Jagirani and Additional Controller Fatima Memon, “no criminal negligence of the institution was found”, the charge sheet said. It noted that Memon and technical instructor Mirza Mursalin Baig were dismissed from their jobs. Similarly, the fire brigade’s Station Officer Zaheer Siddiqui was also dismissed from his role, the charge sheet said, adding that no “criminal negligence was found”. In its report , the Gul Plaza Judicial Commission said the deadly inferno signified a systemic failure across successive provincial and local governments as the legal and administrative mechanisms have existed, but could not be implemented effectively. Justice Agha Faisal of the Sindh High Court (SHC), who headed the commission, noted that the tragic incident was a grave indictment of the failure of municipal and provincial systems to translate legal duties concerning urban safety into effective protection on the ground. It stated that the people not only lost their lives to flames, but also due to delay, darkness, locked exits and windows of the ill-fated building, absence of fire safety systems, unimplemented audits/inspections and fragmented authority. Notably, the commission said KMC, including its fire brigade, Sindh Building Control Authority, Rescue 1122, civil defence department, district administration and others, bore institutional responsibilities for the failure, while material responsibility rested with the people acting as the de facto management of the building together with owners, occupants and commercial operators. The report was handed over to the provincial government months ago but was released last month, apparently against the backdrop of a tragic hospital fire in Islamabad.

Eight Pakistan Bar Council members reject proposed changes to council rules. Eight members of the Pakistan Bar Council (PBC) have rejected proposed amendments seeking to make the council’s proceedings and deliberations confidential, saying the regulatory body of the legal fraternity should instead operate with transparency. In a letter to the PBC secretary, the eight members — Abid Shahid Zuberi, Muhammad Maqsood Buttar, M Shafqat Mehmood-Chauhan, Munir Ahmed Kakar, Abdul Sattar Khan, Salman Akram Raja, Salahuddin Ahmed and Qazi Muhammad Arshad — said all proceedings of the council should be open, since it was an elected body representing the entire legal fraternity. “We are not a private club or some secretive government agency,” the two-page letter said. A copy of the letter was also sent to Attorney General for Pakistan Mansoor Usman Awan, who is the ex-official chairman of the PBC. The letter emphasised that, as a general rule, all proceedings, deliberations and business of the council should be open and transparent and available for scrutiny by the more than 100,000 lawyers it represented, as well as the public at large. The PBC intends to amend Rule 97 of the Pakistan Legal Practitioners and Bar Councils Rules, 1976, by introducing a new Rule 97-A to provide for the confidentiality and classification of proceedings of the council and its committees. Under the proposed rule, all acts, proceedings, deliberations and business of the PBC, its committees, tribunals, sub-committees and other bodies constituted under its authority would be treated as confidential and classified. Such information could not be disclosed, communicated, circulated, published or otherwise made available to any person without the express authorisation of the council or the relevant committee. The proposed amendment also states that no PBC officer, employee, consultant, adviser or any other person with access to the council’s confidential proceedings or records by virtue of their office or functions may disclose, reproduce, transmit, circulate or publish such information, except as otherwise provided under the rules. The confidentiality under this rule will extend to electronic records, emails, electronic communications, audio or video recordings, digital files, photographs, copies and reproductions of any document or proceedings of the council or its committees, the amendment suggested. The members recalled that it was also stated in the Sept 4 letter to the members, which was circulated through WhatsApp, that the rules committee had decided that, since the meeting was not being convened shortly, the amendments should be circulated among the members of the PBC under Rule 91 of the Pakistan Legal Practitioners & Bar Councils Rules, 1976, for their views or approval. The eight members, in their letter, had also drawn the council’s attention to the fact that they had taken strong exception, at the outset, to the manner in which the 1976 rules were sought to be amended, i.e. by way of circular resolution. Firstly, Rule 91 of the 1976 Rules provides that, “in case of emergency”, the PBC may pass a resolution by way of circulation. However, neither the secretary nor the rules committee has explained the “emergency” that requires the overnight amendment of the statutory rules, the letter emphasised, adding that circular resolutions were not a substitute for a proper meeting of the PBC, where the merits and demerits of a proposal could be fully discussed and members would have an opportunity to debate and convince each other. “Unfortunately, there appears to be a trend now in the PBC to pass hugely important and consequential amendments to statutory rules through circular resolutions and bypass the requirement of convening a meeting, even when, clearly, there is no ‘emergency’,” the letter regretted. Besides, under Rule 91, the rules committee has the power, in case of an emergency, to pass a circular resolution instead of convening a meeting of the rules committee itself. However, it has no power to do so in respect of meetings of the council. The rules committee is not the convening authority for the full PBC house, nor can it determine when a full PBC meeting is likely to be held, or decide whether any “emergency” exists, the letter highlighted. The contents of the proposed amendment, however, are even more shocking, the letter stated, as it provides that all acts, proceedings, deliberations and business of the PBC (and any of its committees or other bodies) shall be confidential and classified and shall not be disclosed, circulated or communicated by any PBC member or employee without express permission. The eight members urged all other members to remember that the council was an elected body and its members were statutory representatives of the entire legal fraternity, rather than a “private club or some secretive government agency”. “Therefore, all its proceedings, deliberations and business, as a matter of general rule, must be open, transparent and available for the scrutiny of the more than one lakh lawyers we represent, as well as the public at large.” There may possibly be some limited exceptions to this general rule (for example, in sensitive disciplinary cases involving the privacy of individuals), but the general rule for the PBC must be transparency, the letter emphasised. “Neither we, personally, nor the PBC, collectively, have anything to hide. Unfortunately, this proposed amendment seeks secrecy as the general rule and disclosure and transparency as the exception,” the letter stated. The proposed amendment violates the freedom of speech guaranteed under Article 19 of the Constitution and also violates the right to information guaranteed under Article 19-A of the Constitution, the letter highlighted, rejecting the proposed amendments.

Fresh Yemen clashes kill more than 60: military, medical sources. Fighting between Yemen’s Saudi-backed government forces and the country’s Houthi rebels killed more than 60 people on Saturday, including civilians, medical and military sources told AFP . The renewed clashes in Yemen’s southwest over control of a gateway to the Red Sea came after Friday saw some of the deadliest fighting in years, following the collapse in July of a 2022 ceasefire. According to three Yemeni military sources, 26 government troops were killed during several hours of fighting in the country’s southwest, while medical and military sources from the Houthis said 31 rebel fighters were killed. One medical source in the government-held city of Taiz said a missile strike also killed six civilians travelling by bus and wounded seven others. A government official blamed the strike on the bus, travelling between Taiz and the seat of Yemen’s internationally recognised government in Aden, on the Houthis. In Taiz, a military officer said the “coming hours will be decisive” after the Houthis seized positions near the city a day earlier. The officer added that reinforcements had been arriving from Aden in response to the Houthi offensive, which aims to cut off the government-held port city of Mokha, under fire for weeks, and advance towards areas bordering the Bab al-Mandeb strait . On Friday, the fighting killed 129 people, according to an AFP tally compiled from several sources. With Iran’s closure of the Strait of Hormuz to commercial ships, the Bab al-Mandeb chokepoint has gained importance as a transit route for oil from Saudi Arabia , the world’s biggest exporter of crude. A military official told AFP on Saturday that three airstrikes by Saudi Arabia, a key backer of the government in Aden, had targeted positions recently captured by the Houthis in Taiz. In July, a fragile truce between the Houthis and Yemen’s government fell apart after the rebels welcomed an Iranian plane to the capital Sanaa , setting off a spate of attacks. The fighting between the Houthis and government troops supported by US ally Saudi Arabia signals the emergence of a new front in the wider Middle East war , which broke out in late February with US-Israeli strikes on Iran. The Houthis have also announced a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia and have begun targeting its ships and territory.

Karachi police arrest two over alleged abduction of young man in DHA. KARACHI: Police on Saturday said they had arrested two suspects in connection with the alleged assault of a young man in DHA Phase 8. South Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Syed Asad Raza told Dawn that two of the suspects, Ibrahim Fahad and Waqar, had been arrested in connection with the case. He said a third suspect, Ibrahim Malik, had fled to Lahore, while a fourth, Irtiza, was still absconding. According to the DIG, the incident reportedly stemmed from a dispute involving a girl. The first information report (FIR), a copy of which is available with Dawn , was registered at Sahil police station in the early hours of Saturday on the complaint of Syed Ali Jafri. According to the FIR, the incident took place on the night of Aug 29. The FIR invoked sections 34 (acts done by several persons), 337-A(i) (punishment of shajjah ), 337-V( arsh for hair), 365 (kidnapping or abducting with intent secretly and wrongfully to confine person) and 506-B (criminal intimidation if threat be to cause death or grievous hurt) of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC). Jafri also spoke to the media on Saturday, recalling details of the incident and explaining that the “delay” in getting the FIR registered was because he had been threatened by the suspects against doing so. In his complaint, Jafri said he “remained silent” after the incident as he was scared, but approached the police after the suspects shared his video on social media. Jafri stated that he and his friend had gone to an e-gaming facility in Bukhari Commercial, where his friend’s acquaintance also joined them. He said he had never met the acquaintance before. The three later went to a nearby cafe and, upon leaving, were approached by a vehicle that stopped in front of them. A man, whom Jafri identified as another acquaintance of his friend, then stepped out of the vehicle. The man struck Jafri on the neck with a baseball bat, after which the friend’s acquaintance and “three unknown persons” accompanying him allegedly shoved the complainant into the vehicle and took him to an empty plot at Sahil Avenue in Phase 8, the FIR alleged. He further alleged that he was beaten on his legs with the baseball bat and that his hair was pulled, causing some of it to come out. He was then asked to “eat them”, the FIR said. Jafri said one of the unknown individuals was carrying a gun and that the attackers recorded a video of the assault. According to the FIR, he was shown pictures of his family members and threatened with similar action against them if he complained about the incident. Jafri said he was taken back to Bukhari Commercial in the same vehicle. The complainant also alleged that the suspects demanded Rs30,000 from him. By the time he reached home, he said, one of the individuals involved had already informed his family about the incident. The complainant nominated the three as suspects in the FIR. Last month, a scuffle took place in DHA’s Phase 6 between residents of two apartments, with an inquiry revealing that police officials were involved in the incident and recommending action against them.

JI warns of nationwide wheel-jam strike unless govt provides economic relief. ISLAMABAD: Jamaat-i-Islami (JI) Emir Hafiz Naeemur Rehman on Saturday warned that the party would launch a nationwide wheel-jam strike if the government delayed approving public demands for economic relief. The development came two days after a countrywide protest , during which six party workers were arrested for allegedly burning motorcycles and tyres in Karachi. The JI has distanced itself from these elements. On the same day, Rehman, Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal and Prime Minister’s Adviser Rana Sanaullah announced that the JI and federal government would form committees to recommend measures for reducing the petroleum levy and providing relief to the public. Addressing a news conference in the federal capital alongside JI Deputy Chief Mian Muhammad Aslam and Islamabad Amir Nasrullah Randhawa, Rehman said formal negotiations with the government would begin on Monday, while sit-in protests across the country would continue simultaneously. He also criticised the current administration and bureaucracy, describing them as an unconstitutional “Form-47 arrangement” that was passing the burden of its inefficiency and extravagance on to the public through heavy taxation. Highlighting that the JI had protested for 21 days, with sit-ins held at dozens of locations, including 20 sites in Balochistan and Swat, Rehman maintained that public pressure had forced electricity prices down by Rs10–12 per unit, saved the national exchequer Rs4,300 billion through negotiations with IPPs, and prevented petrol prices from rising further. Addressing the national economic crisis, the JI chief said Pakistan’s total debt had reached Rs110,000bn, while annual interest payments stood at Rs8,000bn. He argued that a three per cent cut in the central bank’s policy rate would eliminate the need for the petroleum levy altogether. Criticising systemic corruption, he highlighted Rs1,300bn in annual losses due to “incompetence” at the Federal Board of Revenue and condemned continued payments to re-gasification plants even when liquefied natural gas was not being supplied. The JI chief also drew attention to governance failures in the social sector, citing a devastating fire at the state-run Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences and a 50pc failure rate in Punjab’s ninth-grade examinations. Rehman criticised Sindh’s key political parties, describing them as “opportunistic” and accusing them of leaving Karachi’s issues unaddressed. He said the grievances had driven residents to demand a separate province. Announcing the party’s future plans, Rehman said the JI would launch a signature campaign targeting 50 million citizens to push for structural relief, local government reforms and a reduction in bread prices to Rs10.

US ambassador says Israel not planning forced displacement from Gaza. The US ambassador to Israel said on Saturday there was no plan underway to force Palestinians out of Gaza, after Israeli ministers laid out ideas on how to expel the war-battered territory’s two million people. “I can tell you categorically there is no plan of the Israelis to displace people out of Gaza against their will,” Ambassador Mike Huckabee told reporters as he visited Palestinian-Americans in the Israeli-occupied West Bank. Israeli far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir laid out a plan on Thursday that aims to see the departure of 250,000 Palestinians from Gaza in the first year, followed by the rest of the roughly two million residents over the following six years. His remarks came a day after Defence Minister Israel Katz said Israel was ready to remove Palestinians from Gaza by sea and land but was waiting for the United States, which he said was discussing where the population would go. Katz, without citing his source, claimed 80 per cent of people in Gaza wanted to leave but that Hamas was preventing them. Huckabee said that President Donald Trump’s administration — which has made hostility to international migration a central priority — wanted to give Palestinians the option to leave by choice. “There is an open-mindedness if people wish to leave, that they should have the right to leave,” Huckabee said, calling it a “disgrace” to “incarcerate” Palestinians inside Gaza. “Nobody is suggesting there would be forced displacement — the Israelis are not, the Americans are not. I know of no one who supports that,” he said. Forced displacement of a civilian population from occupied territory is considered a war crime under the Geneva Conventions. Virtually the entire population of Gaza has already been displaced internally by Israel’s military offensive following the Hamas-led Oct 7, 2023 attack on Israel. Since the war, some far-right Israeli politicians have spoken of bringing settlers back to the Gaza Strip, where Israel dismantled settlements in 2005 as part of a unilateral plan to disengage from the densely populated region. The remarks on displacement come in the run-up to the October 27 elections, in which polls show a tight race for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who has brought once-shunned far-right figures into his cabinet. US President Donald Trump stunned the world early in his second term by proposing to displace all Palestinians at least temporarily from Gaza and turn the rubble-strewn Mediterranean territory into a luxury resort . He backtracked after pushback from countries including Egypt, the only country other than Israel to border Gaza. Israel has ‘responsibility’ to ensure safety of West Bank Palestinians The US ambassador to Israel also said that the Israeli government bore responsibility for West Bank Palestinians’ safety and should impose “severe consequences” over violence, as he visited families after a surge in settler attacks. Mike Huckabee, long known as a staunch supporter of Israel and settlers, visited a Palestinian-American’s home in the West Bank that has been repeatedly targeted by settlers and said he wanted to hear the community’s “legitimate grievances”. As the ambassador met families inside a finely manicured old house in the town of Turmus Ayya , where around 80pc of the 4,000 residents hold US citizenship, a settler from a nearby illegal outpost approached in a quad bike. “One of the messages that we have been sending and we will continue to send is that people in these communities have a right to live with a level of security and safety, and that the government has a responsibility to make sure that that happens,” Huckabee said. Israel has occupied the West Bank since 1967 and violence by Israeli settlers towards Palestinian residents has persisted for years, often with little or no legal consequence, but recent months have seen a surge in attacks ahead of October 27 elections. Huckabee stopped short of criticising Israel by name but said: “Our clear message is that crime is crime, terror is terror. “When people do it they should have an expectation that they will have severe consequences,” Huckabee said. He said that taking action was in the “best interest” of Israel, which already faces growing criticism around the world, including in key ally the United States, over the devastating offensive in Gaza in response to the Oct 7, 2023 Hamas attack. “Their reputation does not do well when it appears that this tiny little group of marauders are somehow representative of the larger population. I don’t believe that it is,” Huckabee said. “There may be a few hundred who are responsible, but that’s a few hundred too many,” Huckabee said. ‘US has the ability’ “We have many issues that we will address,” Nawwaf Zaghoul, the town’s mayor, told reporters ahead of the meeting, describing what he said were constant attacks by settlers. He said that the town’s residents would be asking the ambassador to help secure their safety and security. About 80 per cent of the town’s roughly 3,000 residents were Palestinian Americans, he said. US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee is greeted by members of the local municipality as he arrives to visit the home of an American-Palestinian resident who has previously been twice attacked and faces ongoing harassment from Israeli settlers, in the Israeli-occupied West Bank town of Turmus Ayya, about 23 kilometers northeast of Ramallah, where a large proportion of the town’s residents hold dual nationality on Sept 5, 2026. — AFP Huckabee spent about two hours meeting Palestinian-Americans inside the home of Samir Hazmeh before joining the community in a lunch of maqluba , a dish of rice and meat served after flipping the pot upside down. Hazmeh said the house in which he welcomed Huckabee had its windows smashed twice by settlers, who have also tried to open the gates and burn it down. He has put up both barbed wire and an American flag in hopes of protection. Yasser Alqam, who met the ambassador, owns land just 100 metres away but said he cannot return after several attacks by settlers. “The United States already has the ability to put pressure on Israel to at least arrest those settlers who are known to the authorities,” he said, voicing shock that US President Donald Trump lifted sanctions on settler extremists imposed by predecessor Joe Biden. Alqam’s wife Jinan, wearing a traditional Palestinian dress, said she voiced hope to Huckabee that he “can do something for us and provide us with protection from the settlers so that we can reach our land and pick the olives” in the coming season. Huckabee also visited Taybeh, one of the only Christian villages remaining in the West Bank, in June 2025 after a church there was vandalised . Huckabee said at the time that the desecration of a place of worship was an act of terror and a crime. ‘Thou shalt not steal’ Ahead of elections, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s government has been ramping up approval of new settlements, which are illegal under international law. More than 500,000 Israelis live in the West Bank amid three million Palestinians. Despite Huckabee’s dismissal of violent settlers as a small minority, Netanyahu has brought into his government far-right ministers who have openly mused about expelling the Palestinian population. Huckabee, an evangelical Christian pastor and former governor of Arkansas, has long cited his faith to back Israel and earlier would not even use the term Palestinian. Speaking of violence by settlers, Huckabee said, “I think the Scripture is pretty clear — Thou shalt not steal, thou shalt not kill, and thou shalt not even covet.” Huckabee earlier intervened when settler extremists camped out and blocked basic supplies from reaching another Palestinian-American in the town of Qusra last month, leading to rare condemnation by Netanyahu of settlers. Huckabee refers to the West Bank by its biblical name, Judea and Samaria, a term used by the Israeli government but not adopted by the US government. He has visited Shiloh, a settlement near Turmus Ayya, at least twice since 2025. In February, Huckabee drew widespread condemnation from at least 14 countries , including Pakistan, after he suggested that he would not be opposed to Tel Aviv taking over large swathes of the Middle East.

GB CM constitutes committee to review trekking rules after deadly Broad Peak avalanche. GILGIT: Gilgit-Baltistan Chief Minister Amjad Hussain has constituted a three-member committee to review the 1999 Trekking Rules and Regulations, according to a statement issued by the CM House on Saturday, a few weeks after 10 mountaineers lost their lives when an avalanche struck on Broad Peak . The 10 members were part of an expedition led by world-renowned British-Nepali mountaineer Nirmal Purja . They were struck by the avalanche on July 30. Purja’s company later announced that there were no survivors. CM Hussain expressed deep concern over multiple accidents during mountaineering activities this year, which claimed the lives of 13 foreign climbers including two Pakistanis. In another recent accident, Pakistani clim­ber Asma Mushtaq , 34, died on GB’s Spantik Peak on Aug 20 while desc­ending from the mountain after suffering from high-altitude sickness. A ground team recovered her body on Monday, almost 10 days after her death on the 7,027-metre-tall mountain. The GB chief minister has directed the committee to review the relevant procedures, terms and conditions, and standard operating procedures (SOPs) for dealing with mountaineering incidents. It has also been tasked with determining responsibility for any negligence or administrative lapses in the delayed rescue operations following recent accidents. The committee will be headed by Forest, Wildlife and Parks Secretary Subtain Ahmed, with Information Technology Secretary Zameer Abbas and Baltistan Division Commissioner Kamal Khan serving as members. The CM has further directed the committee to determine responsibility for any shortcomings in the Broad Peak incident, conduct a clause-by-clause review of the existing trekking regulations, and identify outdated, ineffective or incomplete provisions. He also directed the relevant institutions to ensure the safety and security of mountaineers, trekking groups, guides and porters. A source told Dawn that complaints had been submitted to CM Hussain regarding negligence and delay in rescue operations. CM Hussain said it was essential to update regulations concerning permits and registration, briefing and debriefing, the responsibilities of liaison officers and mountain guides, safety equipment, porters’ wages and welfare, insurance, medical facilities and evacuation, communication systems, and emergency response procedures. He specifically directed a review of the existing insurance coverage for liaison officers, mountain guides and porters, adding that realistic and effective insurance coverage should be proposed in view of current risks and costs. He further directed the committee to review arrangements for search and rescue, helicopter evacuation, weather forecasting and early warning systems, communications, and emergency assistance in remote and restricted areas. CM Hussain tasked the committee with developing mandatory safety protocols to minimise the risk of loss of life in the future. The chief minister said that, given the growing popularity of trekking and mountaineering in Gilgit-Baltistan, the existing classification of open and restricted zones, as well as various trekking routes and mountain passes, should also be updated in accordance with ground realities. He said a digital permit and registration system, effective coordination among relevant institutions, and periodic reviews of laws governing the trekking and mountaineering sector were now essential. CM Hussain also reiterated that the GB government would promote mountaineering and tourism in the region without compromising the safety and security of tourists, mountaineers, guides and porters. The committee has been directed to submit a comprehensive report, recommendations and a draft of the proposed amendments to the laws and SOPs to the relevant authority within 15 days. The committee has not yet submitted its report. A government official familiar with the region’s tourism industry told Dawn that the committee had found some tour operators responsible for violating mountaineering rules during the expedition. According to the official, some tour operators had failed to arrange insurance for climbers or helicopters in case of a rescue operation. “Under the rules, if a ground rescue team or helicopter is needed, the tour operator is responsible for arranging a rescue team and paying for helicopter insurance,” the source said. Some operators had also failed to conduct the briefing and debriefing sessions required under the 1999 Trekking Rules, according to the official. In a recent statement, the Alpine Club of Pakistan (ACP) said that search-and-rescue operations relied on government resources, adding that Pakistan lacks a dedicated and properly established high-altitude rescue system. The ACP said that it was working with relevant authorities to develop an effective rescue framework and support improvements to the country’s mountaineering infrastructure. More than 2,200 foreign climbers and trekkers visited GB during the summer season from April to August this year, a senior official of the GB Tourism Department said. Sajid Hussain, deputy director of the GB Tourism Department, told Dawn that foreign adventurers visited the region to scale some of the world’s highest peaks and trek in restricted areas, including K2 (8,611 metres), Nanga Parbat (8,126m), Broad Peak (8,047m), Gasherbrum-I (8,080m) and Gasherbrum-II (8,035m). The official added that a large number of foreign and domestic tourists were currently visiting popular destinations across GB. Foreign tourists visiting open-zone areas do not require permits. Officials further said foreign tourists visiting GB’s tourist destinations and open-zone areas from multiple countries during the spring, summer and autumn seasons were expected to surpass 10,000 this year. GB Tourism Department’s Hussain said the number of foreign adventurers visiting GB this summer was higher than last year . As of June 30, the GB government had earned Rs350 million from expedition and trekking pe­­rmits for this summer.

Inter Board Coordination Commission relaxes equivalence criteria for foreign-board students with two science subjects. ISLAMABAD: The Inter Board Coordination Commission (IBCC) on Saturday decided that Science Group equivalence would be awarded to students of foreign boards who had passed at least two science subjects, providing greater flexibility in academic pathways. Similarly, the forum recommended 12 additional Deeni Madaris for equivalence of their qualifications with SSC and HSSC, bringing the total number of institutions under the equivalence framework to 26. It also agreed to include B-Form/CNIC numbers on SSC and HSSC certificates, making academic records easier to identify, access and verify. Additionally, the commission will offer scholarships and overseas exposure opportunities to board toppers, besides arranging winter and summer camps for high-achieving students to provide them with broader learning, leadership and exposure opportunities. These decisions were made during the 184th IBCC Forum meeting in Murree. “The two-day IBCC Forum concluded in Murree with a series of important decisions aimed at transforming Pakistan’s examination system from rote learning towards conceptual assessment, while improving transparency, uniformity and international recognition of Pakistani qualifications,” a press release said. It added that chairpersons from Boards of Intermediate and Secondary Education (BISEs) across the country, technical education boards, and senior representatives of curriculum and textbook boards had come together for the meeting. According to the press release, National Coordinator of the IBCC Forum Inayatullah Waseem emphasised the importance of active participation and collective ownership of examination reforms. He said the IBCC Forum provided an important national platform for boards to learn from one another, share successful practices and develop common solutions to challenges faced by the examination system. The national coordinator also stressed that greater coordination among boards and consistent implementation of agreed reforms were essential for ensuring fairness, quality and public confidence in examinations across the country. “A major focus of the forum was the implementation of the prime minister’s directives for standardisation of the examination system across the country. The forum adopted measures for greater uniformity in assessment and examination practices, which will also support the credibility and international recognition of Pakistani qualifications,” the press release said. It stated that the forum was informed that examination boards in Sindh, the Federal Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education (FBISE), the AJK Board, the KIU Board, the Aga Khan Board and the Ziauddin Board had implemented the new grading policy, under which the minimum passing marks had been increased to 40 per cent. Awareness sessions and workshops would also be organised to facilitate implementation of the revised grading formula across the country. Meanwhile, the forum agreed to develop a uniform calendar for theory and practical examinations and formulate common guidelines and procedures for practical examinations to ensure greater consistency, fairness and transparency across examination boards. During the meeting, BISE Kohat, BISE Quetta and FBISE presented their best practices, innovative initiatives and outcomes for possible adoption and replication by other boards. Speaking on examination reforms, IBCC Executive Director Dr Ghulam Ali Mallah appreciated the Punjab government for the merit-based appointment of chairpersons of examination boards. He observed that competent professional leadership was adding value to the IBCC Forum and strengthening the national effort to shift examinations from rote learning towards conceptual assessment. Dr Mallah also appreciated the Sindh government and chairpersons of Sindh examination boards for implementing e-marking across the province, describing it as an important step towards greater transparency, efficiency and credibility in the examination system. He emphasised that the reforms being pursued through the IBCC Forum were part of a broader national effort to develop an examination system that tests understanding rather than memory, rewards genuine learning, embraces technology, and strengthens the national and international credibility of Pakistani qualifications.

Suspect in Gizri acid attack case arrested in Punjab: police. A suspect who allegedly attacked a woman with acid in Karachi’s Upper Gizri area recently has been arrested, South Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Syed Asad Raza said on Saturday. A 35-year-old woman suffered burns when a man threw acid on her on Thursday. She was moved to the Burns Centre at Dr Ruth Pfau Civil Hospital Karachi in an Edhi ambulance for treatment. The senior police official said the suspect had fled to his native Rajanpur in Punjab, where he was apprehended with the help of Sindh Police. DIG Raza added that he had written to the Karachi additional inspector general of police to approach the Sindh Home Department for permission to send a police team to Rajanpur and bring the suspect back to Karachi. Police Surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed earlier told Dawn that the victim suffered burns over 15 per cent of her body, affecting her face, neck and abdomen. The victim worked at a bungalow in Clifton and was returning home when the suspect attacked her. Sindh Home Minister Ziaul Hassan Lanjar had taken notice of the incident and had sought an immediate and had directed police to use all available resources to ensure the immediate arrest of the suspect and take legal action to bring him to justice. The Supreme Court in June this year declared acid attacks more heinous than homicide, describing them as crimes that condemn victims to a “living death”.

Brian Lara joins cricket legends in call for proper medical care for Imran Khan. West Indies batting great Brian Lara on Saturday joined an international appeal for proper medical treatment and dignified conditions for imprisoned former Pakistan captain and prime minister Imran Khan, saying the issue was one of “basic humanity”, rather than politics. Last month, 22 international cricketers, including 21 ex-captains, wrote a letter to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif appealing for the ex-premier’s medical treatment in line with recent Supreme Court directives. The letter’s signatories included Michael Atherton, Alex Blackwell, Allan Border, Michael Brearley and Greg Chappell, among others. In a statement posted on his official Instagram account, Lara said he and Imran had crossed paths only a handful of times on the cricket field, but the respect he had for the 1992 World Cup-winning captain was “instant and lasting”. View this post on Instagram “I am struggling to understand how someone who was once a beacon of hope, pride and inspiration for his country, at the height of his sporting career, could now find himself in a situation where he is not being cared for and treated with the compassion and dignity he deserves,” Lara wrote. He said he stood with fellow former international captains in calling for Imran to be provided with “proper, independent medical care and the dignity every human being deserves”. “This isn’t politics. It’s basic humanity for a legend of our game,” Lara said. Imran has been in jail since August 2023, convicted in a string of cases that he says were politically driven following his ouster in a 2022 parliamentary vote. There has been much ado over his health in recent months, with him having been taken to the hospital multiple times for an eye ailment — right central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO) — that came to light in late January. Meanwhile, his party, the PTI, and the government have been engaged in a blame game , with the former accusing the latter of a lack of transparency in not ensuring appropriate treatment for Imran. On August 18, the Supreme Court directed the government to move Imran to Islamabad’s Shifa International Hospital, a private facility, within two days for examination and treatment by a multidisciplinary medical board. However, it later turned out that Imran was instead taken to the government-run Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims). Meanwhile, it was also reported that he could not undergo a recommended computed tomography angiography (CTA) at Pims as the required facilities were unavailable at the hospital.

CDF Munir reaffirms Balochistan’s peace, prosperity central to state efforts: ISPR. Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir on Saturday visited Quetta Garrison, where he reaffirmed that the peace, prosperity and well-being of the people of Balochistan remained paramount for the state. The visit came amid a recent surge in terrorist activity in the province, including attacks in Pishin and Chagai and major counter-terrorism operations in Mastung, Kalat and Sibi over the past week. According to the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), CDF Munir was received by the Quetta Corps Commander upon his arrival and given a comprehensive briefing on the prevailing security environment, operational preparedness and ongoing measures aimed at maintaining peace and stability across Balochistan. “The field marshal reaffirmed that the peace, prosperity and well-being of the people of Balochistan remained central to the efforts of the state,” the ISPR said. “He emphasised that a stable and secure environment would continue to facilitate development initiatives, economic opportunities and improved prospects for the people of the province.” The meeting also covered matters relating to institutional coordination and socio-economic development in the province. CDF Munir appreciated the troops’ high standards of professionalism, operational readiness and commitment. “He underscored the importance of continued coordination among law enforcement agencies and other state institutions to consolidate peace and maintain an environment conducive to sustained economic activity and development,” the statement added. The field marshal also paid tribute to the sacrifices of the martyrs and lauded the troops’ steadfast dedication to the discharge of their duties. Terrorism in Balochistan A day prior, the ISPR said 48 terrorists were killed by security forces in multiple “high-tempo” anti-terror operations across Balochistan over 72 hours. According to the military’s media wing, the operations were carried out in Mastung, Quetta, Kalat and Sibi districts against “Indian proxies, Fitna-al-Hindustan and Fitna-al-Khawarij ”. The state uses the term Fitna-al-Khawarij for the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and has designated Balochistan-based groups as Fitna-al-Hindustan to highlight India’s alleged role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan. On the same day, the Balochistan government issued a statement on the Bhag attack, saying that two policemen were among five people injured as law enforcers foiled a “coordinated” terrorist attack on a police station, bank and the assistant commissioner’s office. Shahid Rind, the chief minister’s aide for political and media affairs, said in a post on X that about 40 terrorists attacked the three places using “heavy weapons, rocket launchers, machine guns, sniper rifles and hand grenades”. Rind said the terrorists failed to take control of the Bhag police station or seize weapons from the facility. Meanwhile, on the night of Aug 31-Sept 1, TTP terrorists launched a coordinated attack on the Customs House, located at Ziarat Cross on the N-50 National Highway, in Pishin district. While security forces responded effectively and killed 10 terrorists, two officers were among six martyred in the exchange of fire, ISPR said. Last month, the security situation remained most severe in Balochistan, where the number of terrorist attacks increased by seven per cent from 83 in July to 89 in August, according to a monthly assessment by the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies (PICSS).

UN agrees text on lethal autonomous weapons. Nearly 130 countries on Saturday agreed on a text defining lethal autonomous weapons systems (LAWS) — “killer robots” to their critics — a first step towards talks on a possible international treaty to regulate them. The text agreed upon has not yet been made public — but campaign groups following the talks have already criticised leading countries for dragging their feet on the issue. Dutch Foreign Minister Tom Berendsen announced the agreement, by 128 countries, on Saturday. The Netherlands has been overseeing the talks. Countries are already developing and using weapons capable of selecting targets and using force against them without human intervention. But the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) warned in a statement that “the unconstrained development and use of autonomous weapon systems pose serious legal, ethical and humanitarian challenges”. The ICRC and several campaigning groups have called for international legally binding rules to restrict and regulate their use. Nicole van Rooijen, executive director of Stop Killer Robots, an international alliance of campaign groups, accused the United States, Russia and their allies of trying to weaken the agreed text. Lex International, a Geneva-based philanthropic group funding work on key policy issues, also criticised some nations’ position. “The United States, Russia, India and Israel are amongst the key opponents of negotiations,” it said. “The governments of Brazil, Ireland, and Norway are leading efforts to get such negotiations started in November.” UN member states will decide at November talks of the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons whether to move towards an international treaty regulating such weapons.

India upend Pakistan for seven-wicket win in Women’s Asia Cup. India brushed Pakistan aside in an emphatic seven-wicket win when the two sides met during the Women’s Asia Cup in Dubai on Saturday, marking India’s seventh Asia Cup triumph against Pakistan in eight matches. Captain Fatima Sana won the toss and chose to bat first, trying to replicate the successful template of Pakistan’s win against Thailand on Tuesday. India captain Harmanpreet Kaur, who became the first player, man or woman to hit the 150-match mark in T20 internationals, said that this was a “good opportunity” for India to bowl first. Both India and Pakistan went with teams unchanged from their previous matches. Steady start Pakistan got off to a chancy yet steady start as opening pair Muneeba Ali and Shawaal Zulfiqaar scored 16 runs in the first three overs. Pakistan were given a reprieve as Muneeba was dropped off the bowling of Kranti Gaud at the beginning of the third over. The pair notched a few boundaries and rotated strike to stitch an opening partnership of 27 runs, when Muneeba, who erroneously gave too much room, was bowled by Shafali Verma for 13 off 15 balls. A spectacular unravelling The bowling change made by captain Kaur to bring Shree Charani on after the initial breakthrough immediately paid dividends as she sent Gul Feroza and Shawaal Zulfiqar back to the dressing room inside the first over of her spell. Gul Feroza came down the track to attempt to hit a turning delivery, but missed the pitch of the ball entirely to send a leading edge to Nadani Sharma at short-third. Shawaal Zulfiqaar fell lbw whilst attempting a sweep at the last ball of the same over. Charani picked up her third wicket as Ayesha Zafar awkwardly miscued a flighted delivery straight into captain Kaur’s hands, reducing Pakistan to 32-4, which became 33-5 as Prema Rawat bowled Sadaf Shamas to conclude the 9th over. Pakistan’s chances to put up a fighting total extinguished all but entirely as captain Fatima Sana, who has often rescued Pakistan from similarly sticky situations in the past, fell lbw for a seven-ball duck to Deepti Sharma. Eyman Fatima and Umm-e-Hani scraped together a ten-run partnership, before a miscommunication at the pitch led to Umm-e-Hani setting off for an unagreed-upon single, causing Eyman to be run out in a scramble to return to the crease, leaving Pakistan reeling at 45-7. The last three wickets amounted for only ten more runs as Umm-e-Hani and Nashra Sandhu fell attempting to chase outside-off deliveries by Rawat, both being caught, for six and zero respectively. Tuba Hassan was the last wicket to fall, with wicketkeeper Richa Ghosh completing a scratchy stumping after Tuba tried playing a Deepti Sharma delivery across the line. Pakistan were bowled out for 55, their lowest ever score in a T20 international match in their 200th outing in the format. Rawat and Charani picked up three poles in each of their extremely economical four-over spells, while Verma and Sharma picked up one and two wickets respectively. Blockbuster start India began what was already considered an easy chase at the onset with thumping conviction, as Shafali Verma hit Sadia Iqbal for a disdainful six off the first ball of the innings. Verma then hit Fatima for a four off the second ball of her spell, before chipping a leading edge off the very next delivery back into Fatima’s hands for an anti-climactic dismissal. Pratika Rawal, in at number three, slashed at a fuller, wider delivery off the Pakistan captain’s bowling. To add to Pakistan’s misery, this reached the fence as it was sloppily handled by Sadia Iqbal at the outfield. Fatima followed a boundary with a wicket for the second time in the same over as she dismissed Rawal caught-behind on the very next delivery to conclude the eventful second over. The skipper struck again to remove India stalwart Smriti Mandhana in her next over for her third wicket, displaying the only symptoms of a fight Pakistan had managed to put up all match. Too little, too late But by then it was all too little, too late for Pakistan, with India only 27 runs away from victory. With the experienced pair of Deepti Sharma and captain Kaur at the crease, India had no reason to hurry – and they played as such, with even the next couple of relatively quiet overs allowing India to close towards the target. Nashra Sandhu and Umm-e-Hani were introduced into the bowling attack, but Pakistan’s abysmal show with the bat had left them with little resistance to potentially offer. Kaur hit Nashra for a four — a chance for Fatima to catch gone begging — and a six to sweetly finish off her milestone appearance for the national team. While Fatima’s haul of three wickets probed at a far-fetched possibility, Pakistan’s complete no-show with the bat had rendered the Green Shirts unable to rally for anything close to a win. Charani was named player of the match; her introduction gave the match its complexion and her pristine figures of three wickets for seven runs further set it in stone. “Important to keep the standards high,” said the Indian captain after the match, adding that all the bowlers played to their strengths and that with Pakistan also bowling a few good deliveries, it was important to see the game through. The Pakistan captain downplayed her three-wicket haul, saying that it “doesn’t matter” as the team lost, and that the side will try to play better cricket in their next fixture. And that they will need to; with India already having qualified for the semi-finals, ensuring that this routing saw them finish top of the group, Pakistan will have to win their next match against Hong Kong to find a spot in the final four.

Putin meets US envoys for Ukraine war talks. Russian President Vladimir Putin began talks with US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff on ending more than four years of war in Ukraine in the Kremlin Saturday, ahead of their first visit to Kyiv expected on Sunday. Both Russia and Ukraine vowed not to strike each other’s capitals for three days during the negotiations, as Washington tries to revive US-led talks to end Europe’s worst conflict since World War Two. US President Donald Trump earlier said his son-in-law Kushner and business ally Witkoff were bringing “a proposal to end the war”. “Dear colleagues, I warmly welcome you to Moscow. The situation is, of course, not simple,” Putin told the envoys in a grand Kremlin hall in footage aired by Russian TV. “But before we begin to address it, I would like to ask everyone to convey their best wishes and words of gratitude to US President Mr Trump.” After talks in Moscow, the pair, sent by US President Donald Trump, are expected to travel on to Kyiv. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky accused Russia of trying to disrupt the envoys’ visit with overnight strikes on Kyiv’s two airports, as well as on a civilian target in the Dnipro region that killed five people. “Clearly, these Russian strikes on the airports are a reaction to the discussions and preparations for the possibility of the US side using an aircraft to travel to Ukraine,” Zelensky said on X, adding there would be “no threats to diplomacy” from the Ukrainian side. It will be the first time that Trump’s businessman friend Witkoff and son-in-law Kushner have visited war-torn Kyiv since Trump returned to office last year with a pledge to resolve the conflict. Travelling to Kyiv by plane would be a highly unusual move, with Ukrainian airspace closed since 2022 because of the war. Visiting leaders and officials have largely travelled by train. The envoys are expected in Kyiv on Sunday, a senior Ukrainian official told AFP , while US outlet Axios reported they would meet Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow on Saturday. Trump told reporters that the two negotiators would seek to gauge whether progress was possible towards peace in the conflict. Peace efforts have stalled due to Washington’s war on Iran , while Moscow and Kyiv have intensified long-range attacks, driving up civilian casualties to levels not seen since the start of fighting. “I sent Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, two great negotiators. They’ve done a great job, and we sent them over to see whether or not we can get something done. And there may be a good chance that we’ll do it,” Trump said. “They’re bringing with them a proposal to end the war.” The US president would not say whether the plan involved Ukraine ceding territory as he has previously suggested, but added: “We have an idea for peace.” Witkoff and Kushner, who have been involved in negotiations for ceasefires in Gaza and Iran, have travelled repeatedly to Moscow in previous attempts at diplomacy. Grinding war The renewed push for diplomacy comes as Russia and Ukraine pummel each other with long-range missile and drone attacks. Just hours before Trump’s announcement on Friday, a Russian drone struck the headquarters of Ukraine’s SBU security service in central Kyiv, according to Zelensky. The strike, which Zelensky said was aimed at the office of the agency’s acting chief, was the first on its headquarters since the start of the invasion. Despite the unprecedented nature of the strike, the Ukrainian president proposed observing a ceasefire with Russia for the duration of the US envoys’ trip. “There will be no airstrikes on our part, and Russia must reciprocally ensure a ceasefire — without its own airstrikes — for the duration needed to conduct these talks,” he said in his evening address. Firefighters work at a site of a Russian drone strike, amid Russia’s attack on Ukraine, in Kyiv region, Ukraine September 3, 2026. — Reuters Russia did not immediately comment on the proposal. Hours later, Oleksandr Ganzha, head of the Dnipropetrovsk regional military administration, said a Russian strike killed four people and wounded five in the southeastern city of Kamianske. Witkoff and Kusher’s trip comes more than a week after a rare visit to Moscow by CIA director John Ratcliffe, who warned Russia against any attack on Nato member states, according to US media. Earlier this week, the United States welcomed the Russian finance minister at a G20 gathering in North Carolina.

Women own just 2pc of land in Pakistan. KARACHI: Only two per cent of women in Pakistan own land, according to a latest survey, highlighting the stark gender gap in land ownership and economic empowerment. The study, carried out by the Sustainable Development Policy Institute (SDPI), revealed that 67pc of Pakistan’s employed women work in agriculture, yet only 1.5pc of agricultural households are formally recorded as female-headed. Land ownership remains equally limited, with only about 2pc of ever-married women aged 15-49 owning land alone or jointly, while 97.2 per cent had not inherited land or a house. According to the study, 99.1pc of women in Sindh do not own land alone or jointly. These barriers are compounded by a significant financial and digital gender gap. SDPI study finds only 1.5pc of agricultural households formally recorded as female-headed Conversely, 56pc of men have a full-service financial account compared with just 14pc of women, while mobile-wallet ownership stands at 48pc among men and 11pc among women. The study says the need for solutions is becoming increasingly urgent as climate risks intensify. Floods in 2022 resulted in more than $30 billion in damage and economic losses, while at least $16.3bn was estimated to be required for resilient reconstruction. The study said half of the country’s population remains largely unrecognised as active agricultural workers. Strengthe­ning the rural economy, particularly agriculture and livestock, was essential to strengthening broader economy, and partnerships with institutions like Mobilink Bank, with their access to large-scale customer data, were vital to sustaining this line of research. The SDPI mentioned that women were doing the agricultural work, absorbing climate shocks and already borrowing to survive, yet the formal financial system did not treat them accordingly. More than nine in 10 women farmers surveyed experienced an extreme climate-related event, including heatwaves, flooding, heavy rainfall or drought-like conditions, over the past five years, while more than 80pc reported crop losses or a negative impact on farming. Borrowing ranked among the first- or second-most common coping strategies across every district. In Khushab, every woman reporting a coping strategy had borrowed money, while more than half had also sold livestock, potentially undermining future income. According to the study, in a country ranked among the world’s most climate-vulnerable, this is not a peripheral issue; it sits at the heart of Pakistan’s agricultural resilience. The exclusion is structural, built into products designed around land ownership, individual mobility and digital access, none of which reflect the reality of women farmers. The findings of the study point to an urgent need for more inclusive, climate-responsive financial solutions that can help women farmers protect livelihoods, recover faster and build greater resilience. The study moves beyond diagnosis to propose a practical framework for designing gender-responsive climate finance, with implications for financial institutions, regulators, development finance institutions and development partners. Published in Dawn, September 6th, 2026

Naqvi doubles down on demand for new provinces. • Interior minister says new units have to be created as population can’t be managed through existing structure • Khawaja Asif says devolution of power ‘inevitable’, accuses major ally of ‘contradictory stance’ • PPP opposes division of Sindh; Rabbani says creating new provinces not a federal matter • PTI asks why PM largely absent from debate LAHORE/KARACHI: Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Saturday renewed his call for a “ reset ” of Pakistan’s governance system, insisting that the country needed to restructure its administrative framework to address decades-old failures in public service delivery and declared that new administrative units had to be made at any cost. “New administrative units will eventually have to be created as Pakistan’s growing population and changing needs can no longer be effectively managed through the existing administrative structure,” said the minister, who is considered close to the powers that be. Addressing a National Policy Dialogue on ‘Devolution of Powers and Good Governance in Pakistan’ at the University of Management and Technology, Mr Naqvi said the proposed “reset” did not mean a change of government or political party but a comprehensive review and restructuring of the administrative system to make it responsive to the needs of citizens. His earlier remarks about “resetting the system” had been widely interpreted as a reference to the incumbent government. He clarified that his call was not aimed at replacing any particular government or political party. Mr Naqvi said Pakistan, after nearly eight decades, was still struggling to provide basic services to its citizens, including education, healthcare, clean drinking water and sanitation. He said Pakistan would eventually have to restructure its administrative boundaries. “New administrative units will have to be created. No one can stop it. However, such a major decision cannot be imposed by an individual or a single political party and should instead be made in accordance with the wishes of the people. If the people want new administrative units, they should be created,” he said. He stressed any restructuring of the state and the creation of new administrative units must take place strictly within the constitutional and legal framework and through political consensus. Drawing an analogy with the growth of a family, the interior minister said that while a single house may once have accommodated an entire family, expanding families eventually required additional homes. “Similarly, as the population grows and its needs increase, the administrative system and structure must also change,” he said. Referring to some political parties, Mr Naqvi said there appeared to be anxiety among certain quarters over devolving powers to the grassroots level, but maintained that such concerns could be addressed through constitutional means. “Powers can be transferred to the lower levels within the framework of the Constitution. No illegal or unconstitutional measures will be permitted,” he said. Provincial status for Islamabad He also called for a debate on granting provincial status to Islamabad, saying residents of the federal capital did not receive a share under the National Finance Commission (NFC) Award. “If new provinces are to be created, Islamabad should also be given the status of a province,” he said and urged political and public support for the proposal. “The opinion of the people is more important than that of politicians on the issue of new administrative units,” he said, adding that no such units should be created without public approval. Khawaja Asif slams ‘double standards’ Defence Minister Khawaja Asif has said that the devolution of power is “inevitable”, while also accusing the PPP of having a contradictory stance on the issue of new provinces. “When there is talk of a Saraiki province in Punjab, the PPP supports it or shows a soft corner on this issue. And when there is talk of multiple provinces or administrative units instead of four, talk of ‘Sindhudesh’ begins,” he said in a post on the social media platform X late Friday night. Mr Asif said that he saw “something else” behind this “dual policy” by the PPP, adding that he would delve into this deeper “when the time comes”. “We are first and foremost Pakistanis. Devolution was decided as a constitutional principle through the 18th Amendment, which was not respected. Time and circumstance demand that it be implemented with integrity,” he said. He said that concentration of power had made the current system obsolete, which needed to be “corrected”. “Provinces or administrative units, whatever label you want to apply. You have 36 divisions, use them, or devise some other administrative-geographical scheme. The devolution of power is inevitable,” he said. PPP opposes Sindh’s division Meanwhile, the PPP stepped up its opposition to the federal government’s statements on new provinces and administrative units. The PPP Sindh leadership, at a meeting chaired by provincial president Nisar Ahmed Khuhro, accused the federal ministers of interfering in the constitutional affairs of the province and warned the federal government against any attempt to undermine Sindh’s autonomy or territorial integrity. The meeting called on Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif to restrain his ministers from making statements on new provinces and warned that continued remarks could lead the PPP to conclude that the federal government was behind a “conspiracy against Sindh’s unity, provincial autonomy and the 18th Amendment”. The PPP Sindh meeting also decided to hold divisional-level ‘Sindh Unity’ seminars and rallies at tehsil headquarters on September 12 under the slogan ‘Sindh is the motherland’.
